send_intents.subject: Building verifiable agents at Proliferate
send_intents.body:
Hi Pablo,

Proliferate's background agents run in isolated sandboxes with internal tool access, but the live multiplayer preview is what stood out to me. Letting engineers inspect and steer a result seems as important as getting an agent to execute.

I built Captor to enforce per-call LLM budgets and tool policies, trace execution, and flag repeated loops. At Stride AI, I also owned backend APIs and complex frontend features. I'd enjoy building both the runtime and the interface that makes its decisions legible.

I'm based in India and open to relocating; the YC Founding Product Engineer listing offers sponsorship. Could I show you a short Captor walkthrough?

Devansh
https://devansh.aurat.ai
https://github.com/8dazo
send_intents.quality_angle: builder-to-builder; sandbox access vs human verification, runtime policy and product UX; contrasts previous agent-reliability email by focusing on live collaborative review.

send_intents.subject: The moment an agent needs a human
send_intents.body:
Hi Yash and Rohan,

Humwork's MCP escalation path addresses a failure I keep seeing: agents loop when they should recognize uncertainty and hand off context. Your matching engine and expert session make that handoff real.

I built Captor around runtime policies, loop detection, and execution traces, and I ship full-stack features and backend APIs. Unlike generic agent wrappers, Humwork treats escalation as core infrastructure. Its mix of MCP tools, matching, and real-time handoff is the founding-engineer work I want.

I'm in India and open to relocating to SF; your YC listing offers sponsorship. Email is the fastest way to reach me. Could I share a Captor walkthrough?

Devansh
https://devansh.aurat.ai
https://github.com/8dazo
send_intents.quality_angle: specific MCP human-escalation and expert matching; loop detection vs previous agent reliability messages, direct question on relevant failure cases.

send_intents.subject: Runtime guardrails and explainable retries at Salus
send_intents.body:
Hi Kevin and Vedant,

Salus's Founding SWE/MLE opening caught my eye because your runtime checks validate agent actions against evidence and policy before execution. The distinction between blocking a bad action and guiding a safe retry is especially interesting.

I built Captor, an SDK for per-call LLM budgets, tool policies, traces, and loop detection. That taught me how easily a guardrail becomes noisy unless its decision is explainable and cheap. I've also shipped backend APIs and full-stack features in production.

I'm based in India and open to relocating; your YC listing offers sponsorship. Could I share a technical walkthrough and learn which enforcement cases you're prioritizing?

Devansh
https://devansh.aurat.ai
https://github.com/8dazo
send_intents.quality_angle: distinguishes evidence-backed pre-action checks from safe retry; connects candidate's Captor guardrails and low-noise explainability.

send_intents.subject: From PTY streams to agent review at Paradev
send_intents.body:
Hi Kiet,

Your October hiring post for Superset, now Paradev, stood out because the founding engineer spans PTY/stream transport through the UI for parallel coding agents. I like that the changelog and source-available repo show how the team actually ships.

At Stride AI I owned backend APIs, complex React interfaces, and end-to-end tests. I also built Captor, a TypeScript SDK for agent budgets, policies, and traces. Making concurrent agent work observable and reviewable is a problem I'd enjoy tackling.

I'm based in India and open to relocating to SF; your careers page explicitly welcomes visa sponsorship. Could I share a repo and discuss the role?

Devansh
